title: K-flat preservation and descent of a supplied scalar chain comparison
statement:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites and compatible small skeletons in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and write $F=g^{-1}$ for inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheafified balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and cochain complexes with the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

For $W=X,Y$ let $j_W:R_W\to S_W$ be a morphism of commutative ring sheaves and let $c_R:FR_Y\simeq R_X$, $c_S:FS_Y\simeq S_X$ be ring isomorphisms with $c_SFj_Y=j_Xc_R$. Write $G_R,G_S$ for the exact module inverse-image functors with actions transported along these isomorphisms, also applied termwise and on ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A good complex means K-flat with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put
$$U(P)=G_RP\otimes_{R_X}S_X,\qquad V(P)=G_S(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y).$$
Assume supplied a natural isomorphism $b:U\simeq V$ on good $R_Y$-complexes, natural for chain maps and compatible with chain homotopies (with $U,V$ acting termwise on the homotopy maps). Then $G_RP$, $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$ and $Z=U(P)$ are good over $R_X,S_Y,S_X$, respectively. Both $U,V$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms between good complexes and induce functors on their homotopy category.

Let $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ denote ordinary derived change of rings, computed by K-flat resolutions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and let brackets denote localization to the relevant derived category. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\beta:C_XG_R\xrightarrow{\sim}G_SC_Y$$
whose component on every flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ is $[b_P]$ under the canonical representative identifications
$$C_XG_RK\simeq[Z],\qquad G_SC_YK\simeq[G_SQ].$$
These identifications include the quasi-isomorphism $G_RP\to G_RK$. The components agree for any two resolutions under the canonical K-flat comparison isomorphisms, compatibly with a third resolution. No flatness of $j_W$, boundedness, derived completeness, or constructibility is required. This assertion descends the supplied $b$; it does not construct a chain comparison or any quotient-tower comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] three times: to the ringed-topos morphism $(g,c_R)$, to the identity topos of $Y$ with ring map $j_Y$, and to the identity topos of $X$ with ring map $j_X$. The first pullback is $G_R$: extension along the ring isomorphism $c_R$ is action transport, via $m\otimes r\mapsto r m$ with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. The other two pullbacks are termwise scalar extension. Consequently $G_RP$, $Q$ and $Z$ are K-flat with flat terms. All sites are small in the stipulated module universe. The cited theorem requires flat terms on the input, which $P$ and then $G_RP$ have; it requires no flatness of the coefficient map. In Lean, obtain the operation-preserving presentation of the actual pro-etale inverse image from lem-sp-proetale-algebraic-inverse-image and its finite-limit preservation from det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image. Transport the functor equality through changeOfRings, including the equality transports on maps. For scalar extension use the identity algebraic inverse image and the supplied model object/map equations.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), applied to coefficient changes and transported inverse image

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], the exact additive functors $G_R,G_S$ preserve all quasi-isomorphisms termwise and have natural derived representative identifications. For a quasi-isomorphism $f:P\to P'$ between good complexes, apply clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to $G_Rf$ over $R_X$ and to $f$ over $R_Y$. Step 1 supplies the required K-flat endpoints. This proves that $U(f)$ and $V(f)=G_S(f\otimes1)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. The functors also pass to homotopy classes: if $f-f'=dh+hd$, their images satisfy the same equation with homotopies $G_Rh\otimes1$ and $G_S(h\otimes1)$, respectively. Additivity and commutation with the differential prove these equalities degree by degree. The supplied homotopy compatibility makes $b$ a natural isomorphism on this homotopy category.

Use lem-pc-kflat-resolution to resolve every complex by a good complex. In the homotopy category, let the resolving predicate mean goodness of the underlying complex. Lift every morphism between good homotopy objects to a chain map using fullness of the homotopy quotient. The supplied chain naturality gives naturality of the conjugated comparison on this resolving class. Apply lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class to extend it to the whole homotopy category; the source functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms because it factors through the derived category. This avoids constructing a second localization model or the two-variable tensor descent.

Put $A=C_XG_R$ and $B=G_SC_Y$. On $\mathcal P$, clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] supply natural isomorphisms $a_P:A([P])\xrightarrow{\sim}[U(P)]$ and $d_P:B([P])\xrightarrow{\sim}[V(P)]$. For $a_P$, first use the exact representative $G_RP$, then compute $C_X$ on this K-flat complex; for $d_P$, compute $C_Y$ on $P$ and then apply the exact representative comparison for $G_S$. Thus $t_P=d_P^{-1}[b_P]a_P$ is a natural isomorphism $A\ell\cong B\ell$. Naturality follows by composing the three natural squares, for every homotopy class of chain maps. The normalization uses the supplied $b$, without constructing another tensor comparison.

proof.text: Apply the fully faithful restriction along DerivedCategory.Qh, supplied by lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property, to descend the transformation constructed from the resolving class. It is invertible on good complexes by its formula; naturality along resolutions proves invertibility on every complex, and essential surjectivity of DerivedCategory.Q proves invertibility everywhere. For uniqueness, compare on each good resolution and cancel the image of its quasi-isomorphism, then use Localization.natTrans_ext along DerivedCategory.Q. No arbitrary choice enters the resulting uniquely normalized isomorphism.

proof.text: For any good resolution $s:P\to K$, the exactness result [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] makes $G_Rs$ a quasi-isomorphism, so clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes $C_XG_RK$ using $G_RP$. More explicitly set $a_s=a_P A([s])^{-1}:A([K])\xrightarrow{\sim}[U(P)]$ and $d_s=d_P B([s])^{-1}:B([K])\xrightarrow{\sim}[V(P)]$. Naturality of $\beta$ gives $d_s\beta_{[K]}a_s^{-1}=[b_P]$. If $s':P'\to K$ is another resolution, the source comparison is $a_{s'}a_s^{-1}$ and the target comparison is $d_{s'}d_s^{-1}$. Substituting the displayed formula gives $(d_{s'}d_s^{-1})[b_P]=[b_{P'}](a_{s'}a_s^{-1})$. These are the canonical K-flat comparisons of the cited change-of-rings theorem, since each is formed from its representative maps and the inverses of the resolution isomorphisms. For a third resolution the composites cancel the intermediate $a_s$ and $d_s$, proving the cocycle compatibility. Nothing used boundedness, completeness, constructibility or flatness of $j_W$.
